public_rationale: The contract asks whether frontier models had substantial hallucination rates around April–May 2025, and whether harmful fabrication incidents were still happening then. Both parts are met. OpenAI's system card of April 16, 2025 reported PersonQA hallucination rates of 33% for o3 and 48% for o4-mini, against 16% for the older o1. It reported SimpleQA rates of 51% and 79%. OpenAI wrote that more research was needed to understand the cause. On the same date, Transluce reported that o3 often made up actions it had taken and justified them when challenged. It said this behaviour also appeared in o3-mini and o1. On May 22, 2025, an LA Times column reported that Damien Charlotin's list held 99 court cases with AI hallucinations. It said that in some 30 cases involving lawyers, the errors were found or filed as recently as that year. No evidence in the packet shows that the problem had been solved by May 2025. 'Deep' and 'serious' are judgments, but the evidence fits the plain reading.
limitations: Hallucination rates depend heavily on the benchmark and the model. The cited figures come from a few evaluations and do not give one general rate.
The court-case counts cover only publicly reported cases and do not measure how often hallucinations happen overall.

our_interpretation: Read as a claim about the state of generative AI at the post date (May 2025): leading models still hallucinated at material rates, and no developer had shown a fix.

'Deep, serious' is a judgment. Plain reading: material hallucination rates on published evaluations from leading labs, plus documented real-world harm. 'Unsolved' means no lab claimed or showed that hallucinations had been eliminated.
The part about warning since 2001 is biographical and is not scored.
